title: 全球最深湖泊
source_line: 数据：湖泊测量与研究论文、国际湖泊环境委员会（ILEC）、联合国粮农组织（FAO）、美国地质调查局（USGS）等

items.name: 贝加尔湖
items.subtitle: 俄罗斯西伯利亚
items.image_hint: Lake Baikal, Siberia, Russia: the classic views are Olkhon Island with Shaman Rock (Cape Burkhan) or the famous clear turquoise winter ice with frozen bubbles and cracks; must be Baikal, not another frozen lake

source.name: INTAS Project 99-1669 'A New Bathymetric Map of Lake Baikal' (Oct 2002)
source.method: Digital map from Russian Navy echo-sounding of the whole lake (1979–1987) plus seismic lines; 1,642 m is 5 m deeper than the Pisces submersible value (1,637 m).

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Older figures: 1,620 m (1960s charts), 1,637 m (Pisces submersible, 1990), 1,741 m (unconfirmed 1931 estimate, still printed in the ILEC databook). Floor 455.5 - 1,642 = -1,186.5 m: about 1,187 m below sea level.

items.name: 坦噶尼喀湖
items.subtitle: 东非大裂谷
items.image_hint: Lake Tanganyika shoreline: steep green rift-valley mountains dropping into the lake (Mahale Mountains or Kigoma, Tanzania, or the DR Congo / Burundi shore), wooden fishing boats; must be Tanganyika, not Lake Malawi or Lake Victoria

source.name: FAO Lake Tanganyika Research (GCP/RAF/271/FIN), 'Characteristics of Lake Tanganyika' (1999)
source.method: Soundings of the Belgian Hydrobiological Exploration 1946–47 (Capart 1949): deepest 1,470 m in the southern trough, 1,310 m in the northern trough.

cross_check.name: ILEC World Lake Database: Lake Tanganyika (table 1,471 m; text 1,470 m)

items.notes: Shared by DR Congo (14,800 km², 45%), Tanzania (13,500 km², 41%), Burundi (8%) and Zambia (6%) per the FAO LTR table; flag = largest area share (DR Congo). Wikipedia's article gives Tanzania 46% / DRC 40% (not used: the FAO figure is the primary project source). Wikipedia text places the maximum in the northern basin, contradicting FAO and the 1949 report (southern trough).

items.name: 里海
items.subtitle: 欧亚交界
items.image_hint: Caspian Sea coast in Kazakhstan, e.g. the white chalk cliffs and turquoise water of the Mangystau coast near Aktau; a natural coastline, not a city skyline, not the Aral Sea

source.name: Abai Institute / Kazakhstan government portal 'Caspian Sea' (max depth 1,025 m)
source.method: South Caspian Basin, east of the Kura delta; value from Soviet hydrographic surveys (Kosarev & Yablonskaya 1994 give 1,024–1,025 m).

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Counted as a lake (endorheic salt lake, the convention used by geographers and by Wikipedia's list); some treat it as a sea, and its deep basin is oceanic crust. No agreed division of the water surface exists, so the flag goes to the country with the longest shoreline: Kazakhstan, 2,340 of ~7,000 km (oq.gov.kz). Continent: Asia (4 of 5 littoral states are Asian; the lake straddles the Europe–Asia line).

items.name: 奥希金斯湖／圣马丁湖
items.subtitle: 巴塔哥尼亚，智利与阿根廷交界
items.image_hint: Lago O'Higgins, Aysén, Chile: milky turquoise glacial lake with the O'Higgins Glacier calving front and icebergs, Southern Patagonian Ice Field; not Lago Argentino or Perito Moreno

source.name: Minowa, Schaefer & Skvarca 2023, J. Glaciology 69(278) (CC BY 4.0)
source.method: Boat echo-sounding, February 2020: deepest point ~41 km along the centreline, near the O'Higgins Glacier.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Long quoted as 836 m (CECS 2003/2010 press figure; Spanish Wikipedia still shows it). The 2023 peer-reviewed survey measured 799 m, 'similar to Schaefer and others (2011)'. Area: Chile 554 km², Argentina 459 km² (Spanish Wikipedia) -> Chile flag.

items.name: 别德马湖
items.subtitle: 巴塔哥尼亚圣克鲁斯省
items.image_hint: Lago Viedma, Santa Cruz, Argentina: the Viedma Glacier front and icebergs on the lake, or the lake with the Fitz Roy massif behind it near El Chaltén; not Lago Argentino or Perito Moreno

source.name: Minowa, Schaefer & Skvarca 2023, J. Glaciology 69(278) (CC BY 4.0)
source.method: Boat echo-sounding Jan 2017 – Jun 2020 (merged with earlier soundings) near the Viedma Glacier: 'the deepest part of the lake was ~750 m deep'.

cross_check.name: CONICET press release 21 Jul 2022 (Lenzano et al., survey May 2022)

items.notes: Disputed. CONICET/UNCuyo announced ~900 m (±3%) after a May 2022 survey near the retreating glacier front, but no peer-reviewed bathymetry with that value was found; the 2023 peer-reviewed survey gives ~750 m. We rank by ~750 m and show '~'. If 900 m were confirmed Viedma would move to #4 (above O'Higgins). The deep trench was under glacier ice until recent retreat.

items.name: 马拉维湖
items.subtitle: 又称尼亚萨湖
items.image_hint: Lake Malawi from the Malawi shore: Cape Maclear / Lake Malawi National Park granite boulders and clear water, or Likoma Island beach; not Lake Tanganyika

source.name: ILEC World Lake Database: Lake Malawi (Nyasa) databook
source.method: Single basin, 'greatest depth of about 706 m near the western shore about 45 km north of Nkhata Bay'.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Shared by Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania; the Malawi–Tanzania boundary is disputed (Malawi claims the water up to the Tanzanian shore). Malawi administers by far the largest part of the surface and the deepest point lies off its western shore -> Malawi flag.

items.name: 伊塞克湖
items.subtitle: 吉尔吉斯斯坦天山山脉
items.image_hint: Issyk-Kul lake, Kyrgyzstan: deep blue water with the snow-capped Tian Shan (Teskey or Kungey Ala-Too) ranges behind, e.g. from the south shore near Tamga or Bokonbayevo; not Song-Kul

source.name: De Batist et al. 2001, echo-sounding bathymetry of Issyk-Kul (cited by Zavialov et al. 2018, HESS 22:6279)
source.method: High-quality echo-sounding survey; Zavialov et al. judge 668 m the most plausible value and 702 m (still common online) unsupported.

cross_check.name: ILEC World Lake Database: Lake Issyk-Kool

items.notes: 702 m appears in Russian Wikipedia and some older works (Alamatov & Mikkola 2011); not used.

items.name: 大奴湖
items.subtitle: 西北地区
items.image_hint: Great Slave Lake, Northwest Territories, Canada: rocky Canadian Shield shoreline and islands of the East Arm or Yellowknife Bay, clear summer day or aurora over the lake; not Great Bear Lake

source.name: The Canadian Encyclopedia: 'Great Slave Lake' (614 m in Christie Bay)
source.method: Maximum recorded depth 614 m in Christie Bay (East Arm); Tulaczyk's 2005–06 soundings suggest trenches up to ~30 m deeper (Spectacular NWT).

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Deepest lake in North America by maximum depth. No modern full bathymetric survey was found; the value may be an underestimate.
items.image_note: 图片授权不明，暂不展示

items.name: 阿根廷湖
items.subtitle: 巴塔哥尼亚圣克鲁斯省
items.image_hint: Lago Argentino, Los Glaciares National Park, Argentina: the Perito Moreno Glacier ice wall rising from the milky turquoise lake (classic view from the Magallanes peninsula boardwalks), or icebergs from the Upsala Glacier

source.name: Minowa, Schaefer & Skvarca 2023, J. Glaciology 69(278) (CC BY 4.0)
source.method: Brazo Upsala arm (where Wikipedia locates the deepest point): 'The deepest part of the lake with a depth of 607 m'. Earlier surveys 2012–14 gave 560–580 m.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia 'Lake Argentino' (719 m, citing a dead uncuyo.edu.ar page)

items.notes: Disputed. 719 m (Wikipedia, source link dead, not verifiable) vs 607 m (peer-reviewed survey of the same Upsala arm) vs ~500 m (older Spanish sources). EGU 2022 abstract (Van Wyk de Vries et al.) cored at water depths 'up to 600 m'. We use the deepest published sounding, 607 m; with 719 m it would rank #6.

items.name: 火山口湖
items.subtitle: 俄勒冈州喀斯喀特山脉
items.image_hint: Crater Lake, Oregon, USA: the deep-blue caldera lake with Wizard Island seen from the rim, clear sky; not another crater lake

source.name: USGS: 'Bathymetry and the Floor of Crater Lake'
source.method: Multibeam sonar survey, summer 2000 (Bacon et al. 2002, GSA Bulletin): new maximum depth 594 m / 1,949 ft.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: The National Park Service quotes 592 m (different surface elevation datum). Deepest lake in the United States.

items.name: 马塔诺湖
items.subtitle: 南苏拉威西省
items.image_hint: Lake Matano near Sorowako, South Sulawesi, Indonesia: very clear blue water over the shallows with forested hills; not Lake Toba or Lake Towuti

source.name: Crowe et al. 2008, Limnology & Oceanography 'The biogeochemistry of tropical lakes: a case study from Lake Matano' (via Wikipedia)
source.method: Maximum depth 590 m (bathymetry after Herder et al. 2006), as cited in Wikipedia.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Deepest lake in Indonesia and on any island. Primary paper not opened directly (via Wikipedia citation).
items.image_note: 图片授权不明，暂不展示

items.name: 卡雷拉将军湖
items.subtitle: 又称布宜诺斯艾利斯湖
items.image_hint: Lago General Carrera, Aysén, Chile: the Marble Caves (Capillas de Mármol) with turquoise water, or the vivid turquoise lake from the Carretera Austral; must be this lake

source.name: Murdie et al. 1999, Geo-Marine Letters 18:315–320; IRD extended abstract (4th ISAG, 1999)
source.method: Heat-flow and echo-sounding bathymetry survey (1998).

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Spanish Wikipedia says 590 m (uncited). Area: Chile 978 km² (52.8%, Muñoz et al. 2006), Argentina 872 km² -> Chile flag. Primary not opened directly (IRD link redirects).

items.name: 霍宁达尔湖
items.subtitle: 挪威韦斯特兰郡
items.image_hint: Hornindalsvatnet, Vestland, Norway: long dark-green lake between steep forested mountains near Grodås / Hornindal, calm reflections; not a sea fjord

source.name: Seppälä 2005, The Physical Geography of Fennoscandia (Oxford UP), p.145; NVE lake database
source.method: NVE depth maps (echo sounding). Via Wikipedia citation.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Deepest lake in Europe (Wikipedia 'Greatest maximum depth by continent'); surface 53 m, so the floor is ~461 m below sea level.
items.image_note: 图片授权不明，暂不展示

items.name: 克内尔湖
items.subtitle: 不列颠哥伦比亚省
items.image_hint: Quesnel Lake, Cariboo, British Columbia, Canada: long forested fjord-like lake with mountains, e.g. near Likely or the North Arm, aerial or shoreline view

source.name: Petticrew et al. 2015, Geophysical Research Letters 42, p.3349 (via Wikipedia)
source.method: Bathymetry used in the Mount Polley tailings-spill study.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Some older lists give 506 m. Claimed as the deepest fjord lake in the world (Potts 2004).
items.image_note: 图片授权不明，暂不展示

items.name: 多巴湖
items.subtitle: 北苏门答腊省
items.image_hint: Lake Toba, North Sumatra, Indonesia: the huge caldera lake with Samosir Island seen from a high viewpoint (e.g. Sipinsur or Huta Ginjang), green hills

source.name: LakeNet / World Lakes Database (via Wikipedia 'Lake Toba')
source.method: Value as cited by Wikipedia.

cross_check.name: ILEC World Lake Database: Lake Toba

items.notes: ILEC gives 529 m (4.8% higher); with 529 m Toba would rank #13. Kept at 505 m (most widely used; ILEC databook data are older). Largest volcanic lake on Earth; caldera of the ~74,000-year-old Toba super-eruption.

items.name: 萨雷兹湖
items.subtitle: 戈尔诺-巴达赫尚自治州，帕米尔高原
items.image_hint: Sarez Lake, Pamir Mountains, Tajikistan: long turquoise mountain lake between barren high peaks, possibly the Usoi landslide dam; remote, not Karakul or Iskanderkul

source.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)
source.method: No primary bathymetry found; the Wikipedia article gives 505 m without a citation.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia 'Sarez Lake' infobox

items.notes: Weakly sourced value (commonly 'about 500 m'). Natural lake: formed in 1911 when an earthquake-triggered landslide (the Usoi Dam, tallest natural dam) blocked the Murghab River. Surface 3,263 m, so even its deepest point is ~2,758 m ABOVE sea level.

items.name: 太浩湖
items.subtitle: 加利福尼亚州与内华达州交界
items.image_hint: Lake Tahoe, California/Nevada, USA: Emerald Bay with Fannette Island, or crystal-clear water over granite boulders on the east shore (Sand Harbor)

source.name: USGS Lake Tahoe Data Clearinghouse, 'Facts about Lake Tahoe' (1,645 ft; 1998 multibeam survey)
source.method: USGS multibeam bathymetry, 1998.

cross_check.name: ILEC World Lake Database: Lake Tahoe

items.notes: 1,645 ft = 501.4 m. Lies in two US states, one country (no SHARED badge).

items.name: 萨尔瓦特湖（Salvatnet）
items.subtitle: 挪威特伦德拉格郡
items.image_hint: Salvatnet lake near Salsbruket, Namsos, Trøndelag, Norway: narrow lake between steep forested hills; must be Salvatnet (Salsvatnet)

source.name: Seppälä 2005, The Physical Geography of Fennoscandia (Oxford UP), p.145
source.method: Modern echo sounding 482 m; old manual method 464 m (Wikipedia 'Salvatnet').

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Surface only 9 m above sea level: floor ~473 m below sea level.

items.name: 基伍湖
items.subtitle: 阿尔伯特裂谷
items.image_hint: Lake Kivu: green terraced islands and calm water at Kibuye/Karongi or Gisenyi (Rwanda side) or Goma/Bukavu (DR Congo side), fishermen's boats; not Lake Tanganyika

source.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291) / Wikipedia 'Lake Kivu' infobox
source.method: No primary bathymetry opened; the article body cites 475 m, French Wikipedia 485 m.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia 'Lake Kivu' body text

items.notes: Values in circulation 475–485 m; at 485 m it would swap with Salvatnet (482 m). Flag: DR Congo by convention (first-listed, larger share of the lake per common descriptions; no published split checked) — to confirm.

items.name: 纳韦尔瓦皮湖
items.subtitle: 巴塔哥尼亚巴里洛切
items.image_hint: Nahuel Huapi Lake, Bariloche, Argentina: the classic view from Cerro Campanario over the lake arms, islands and Andes, or Llao Llao; natural landscape

source.name: Wikipedia 'Nahuel Huapi Lake' (maximum measured depth as of 2007)
source.method: Measurement reported as of 2007; primary survey not found.

cross_check.name: AFS 2011 conference abstract 'Fish distribution in a deep ... lake of Patagonia'

items.notes: Other figures: 438 m (older Wikipedia), ILEC '<300 m'. 464 m kept as the most recent measured value.

items.name: 豪鲁卡湖
items.subtitle: 南岛峡湾地区
items.image_hint: Lake Hauroko, Fiordland National Park, New Zealand: remote lake with dense native beech forest and steep mountains, mist; not Lake Te Anau or Manapouri

source.name: Wikipedia 'Lake Hauroko' (cites Te Ara 'New Zealand lakes', Nathan 2007; Southland Times 2014)
source.method: Value as given in the article and its cited NZ sources (not opened directly).

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: New Zealand's deepest lake (Southland Times 2014; Te Ara).
items.image_note: 图片授权不明，暂不展示

items.name: 科克伦湖／普埃雷东湖
items.subtitle: 巴塔哥尼亚，智利与阿根廷交界
items.image_hint: Lago Cochrane, Aysén, Chile: intensely turquoise lake near the town of Cochrane / Tamango National Reserve with dry hills; Argentine side is Lago Pueyrredón

source.name: Murdie et al. 1999 (IRD extended abstract; Geo-Marine Letters)
source.method: 'the central basin of the lake reaches a depth of 460 m'.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Area: Chile 175 km², Argentina 150 km² (Wikipedia) -> Chile flag.

items.name: 廷湖
items.subtitle: 挪威泰勒马克郡
items.image_hint: Tinnsjøen (Lake Tinn), Telemark, Norway: long lake squeezed between steep mountains, e.g. near Mæl or Hovin; not Mjøsa

source.name: Seppälä 2005, The Physical Geography of Fennoscandia (Oxford UP), p.145
source.method: Via Wikipedia citation.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Site of the 1944 sinking of the heavy-water ferry SF Hydro.
items.image_note: 图片授权不明，暂不展示

items.name: 亚当斯湖
items.subtitle: 不列颠哥伦比亚省
items.image_hint: Adams Lake, Shuswap region, British Columbia, Canada: long forested mountain lake, summer, shoreline or aerial view

source.name: BC Government page 'Adams Lake' (via Wikipedia)
source.method: Value as cited by Wikipedia to gov.bc.ca.

cross_check.name: Cal-Eco Consultants 2006 (via Wikipedia)

items.notes: Disputed: another account gives 397 m (would drop it out of the 400 m club). Kept at 457 m as given by the provincial source.
items.image_note: 图片授权不明，暂不展示

items.name: 奇兰湖
items.subtitle: 华盛顿州
items.image_hint: Lake Chelan, Washington, USA: long narrow blue lake winding between the North Cascades mountains, e.g. from Chelan Butte or near Stehekin

source.name: Washington State Dept. of Ecology reports (via Wikipedia 'Lake Chelan')
source.method: 1,486 ft = 452.9 m, Lucerne basin.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Natural glacial lake; the 1927 Lake Chelan Dam raised its level by 21 ft (~6.4 m) (Wikipedia). Still a natural lake, so included; without the raise the depth would be ~447 m and the rank unchanged.

items.name: 米约萨湖
items.subtitle: 挪威内陆郡
items.image_hint: Mjøsa, Norway's largest lake, Innlandet: wide lake with rolling farmland and forest shores, e.g. near Lillehammer or Gjøvik, possibly with the paddle steamer Skibladner

source.name: NVE (Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate), 'Dybdekart for Mjøsa' (1984)
source.method: Official echo-sounding depth chart.

cross_check.name: ILEC World Lake Database: Lake Mjøsa

items.notes: ILEC (older) gives 449 m.

items.name: 凡湖
items.subtitle: 安纳托利亚东部
items.image_hint: Lake Van, eastern Turkey: deep blue lake with the snow-capped Süphan or Nemrut volcano behind; natural view (avoid close-ups of Akdamar church)

source.name: Degens, Wong, Kempe & Kurtman 1984, Geologische Rundschau 73:701–734
source.method: Echo-sounding and seismic survey; deepest in the Tatvan basin.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Saline soda lake (world's largest saline soda lake per the Zoosystematics and Evolution paper cited by Wikipedia); deepest part is the Tatvan basin.

items.name: 大熊湖
items.subtitle: 西北地区

tags.text: 完全位于加拿大的最大湖泊

items.image_hint: Great Bear Lake, Northwest Territories, Canada: vast Arctic lake with low tundra/taiga shores, clear water, summer light; not Great Slave Lake

source.name: Johnson 1975, J. Fish. Res. Board Can. 32:1971–1987
source.method: Physical survey of Great Bear Lake.

cross_check.name: ILEC World Lake Database: Great Bear Lake

items.notes: Largest lake lying entirely within Canada (ILEC; Superior and Huron have larger Canadian parts but are shared).

items.name: 玛纳普利湖
items.subtitle: 南岛峡湾地区
items.image_hint: Lake Manapouri, Fiordland, New Zealand: forested islands and mountains seen from Frasers Beach or Pearl Harbour; not Te Anau

source.name: Wikipedia 'Lake Manapouri' (New Zealand's second-deepest lake, 444 m)
source.method: Value as given in the article (source not opened directly).

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: New Zealand's second-deepest lake.

items.name: 科莫湖
items.subtitle: 意大利伦巴第大区
items.image_hint: Lake Como, Lombardy, Italy: classic view of the lake and mountains from Bellagio or Varenna, villas on the shore, blue water

source.name: Istituto Italiano di Idrobiologia (CNR), 'Laghi italiani'
source.method: Italian national limnology institute table.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: One of the deepest lakes in Europe; floor ~227 m below sea level.

items.name: 蒂阿瑙湖
items.subtitle: 南岛峡湾地区
items.image_hint: Lake Te Anau, Fiordland, New Zealand: lake with the Murchison/Kepler mountains, from the Te Anau lakefront or Kepler Track; not Manapouri

source.name: NZ Ministry for the Environment (via Wikipedia); Lowe & Green 1987
source.method: Value as listed.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Largest lake in the South Island.

items.name: 田泽湖
items.subtitle: 本州秋田县
items.image_hint: Lake Tazawa, Akita, Japan: round caldera lake with intensely blue water and forested shores; avoid close-ups of the golden Tatsuko statue (sculpture copyright)

source.name: Wikipedia 'Lake Tazawa' (423.4 m; 1937–40 survey by Yoshimura found 425 m)
source.method: Successive surveys: 397 m (1909, hemp rope), 413 m (1926), 425 m (1937–40).

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Deepest lake in Japan (Shikotsu 363 m second).

items.name: 汉泰湖（Khantayskoye）
items.subtitle: 西伯利亚克拉斯诺亚尔斯克边疆区
items.image_hint: Lake Khantayskoye, Putorana Plateau, Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia: remote Arctic lake below flat-topped basalt plateau cliffs and waterfalls; Putorana scenery, must be this region

source.name: Great Soviet Encyclopedia 'Хантайское озеро' (via Wikipedia)
source.method: Soviet-era survey value.

cross_check.name: RBTH '10 of Russia's deepest lakes'

items.notes: Remote lake on the edge of the Putorana Plateau, above the Arctic Circle. Only Soviet-era data.

items.name: 格雷湖
items.subtitle: 智利百内国家公园
items.image_hint: Lago Grey, Torres del Paine National Park, Chile: blue icebergs floating on grey-turquoise water with Grey Glacier and the Paine massif; not Lago Pehoé

source.name: Sugiyama et al. 2021, Nature Communications 12, 6301 (CC BY 4.0)
source.method: 'Lago Grey, a 410-m-deep glacial lake'; moorings to 392 m.

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of lakes by depth (rev 1371850291)

items.notes: Fed by Grey Glacier, Southern Patagonian Ice Field.

items.name: 苏必利尔湖
items.subtitle: 五大湖地区

tags.text: 全球面积最大的淡水湖

items.image_hint: Lake Superior: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore cliffs (Michigan, USA) with clear turquoise water, or the rugged north-shore cliffs; must be Lake Superior

source.name: US EPA 'Great Lakes: Physical Facts' (1,333 ft)
source.method: NOAA/EPA charted depth; deepest point reached by J. Val Klump's submersible, 30 Jul 1985.

cross_check.name: ILEC World Lake Database: Lake Superior

items.notes: Shared by the USA (Michigan, Wisconsin, Minnesota) and Canada (Ontario); flag: USA by the larger share of the surface (convention; not re-measured) — to confirm. Largest freshwater lake by area.

insights.text: 旧榜波索湖450米、瓦卡蒂普湖420米，实测395米、约380米，均落榜。
下一个萨雷兹湖，源于1911年地震引发的滑坡堵住帕米尔河流。
前10名有3个巴塔哥尼亚湖泊，塑造它们的冰川至今仍在退缩。
下一个别德马湖：2022年测称900米未发表，同行评审声呐测深约750米。
接下来第1名：储有全球约20%的未冻结淡水（联合国教科文组织）。

scope_note: 收录标准：最大实测深度超过400米的天然湖泊，按该深度排名，单位为米。因小型水坝而抬高水位的天然湖泊（如奇兰湖）计入；水库及沃斯托克湖等冰下湖不计入。里海按湖泊计算。测量结果不一致时，采用最新发表的测深结果，并标注“深度有争议”。跨国湖泊展示湖泊面积占比最大国家的国旗；里海按岸线最长的国家展示，但其最深点位于南里海。深度相同则并列。
